question: How many customers are there?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers

question: List the names of all products.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products

question: Show the names of customers who live in Delhi.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = 'Delhi'

question: What is the price of the most expensive product?
expected_sql: SELECT MAX(price) FROM products

question: How many products are in the Electronics category?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics'

question: Show the names of products that cost more than 100.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price > 100

question: What is the average price of all products?
expected_sql: SELECT AVG(price) FROM products

question: How many orders have been placed in total?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders

question: Which distinct cities do our customers live in?
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers

question: What is the total quantity of products ordered across all orders?
expected_sql: SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM orders

question: How many customers are there in each city? Show the city and the count.
expected_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY city

question: What is the average product price in each category? Show the category and the average price.
expected_sql: SELECT category, AVG(price) FROM products GROUP BY category

question: Show the names and prices of the 5 most expensive products, most expensive first.
expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5

question: How many orders has each customer placed? Show the customer name and the number of orders, only for customers who have placed at least one order.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name

question: What is the total quantity ordered for each product category? Show the category and the total quantity.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.quantity) FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.category

question: Which customers placed an order in August 2026? Show their names without duplicates.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.order_date LIKE '2026-08%'

question: Which cities have more than 3 customers? Show only the city names.
expected_sql: SELECT city FROM customers GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) > 3

question: List the product names sorted by price from lowest to highest.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products ORDER BY price ASC

question: How many orders were placed in each month? Show the month as YYYY-MM and the number of orders.
expected_sql: SELECT substr(order_date, 1, 7), COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY substr(order_date, 1, 7)

question: What is the total revenue across all orders, where revenue is product price times quantity?
expected_sql: SELECT SUM(p.price * o.quantity) FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id

question: Which customers have never placed an order? Show their names.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)

question: Which products have never been ordered? Show their names.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM orders)

question: Show the names and total spending of the top 5 customers by total spending, highest first. Spending is price times quantity.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 5

question: Which product category generates the most revenue? Show the category and its total revenue.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

question: Which customers have a total spending above the average total spending of customers who have placed orders? Show their names.
expected_sql: WITH spend AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name) SELECT name FROM spend WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM spend)

question: For each city, show the city and the total revenue from its customers' orders, highest revenue first.
expected_sql: SELECT c.city, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY revenue DESC

question: What is the name of the product with the highest total quantity ordered?
expected_sql: SELECT p.name FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY SUM(o.quantity) DESC LIMIT 1

question: Show each customer's name and the date of their most recent order, only for customers who have placed orders.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, MAX(o.order_date) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name

question: Which customers have bought products from more than one category? Show their names.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 1

question: What percentage of total revenue comes from the Electronics category? Round to 2 decimal places.
expected_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.category = 'Electronics' THEN p.price * o.quantity ELSE 0 END) / SUM(p.price * o.quantity), 2) FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id
